story: At midday on a sunny Sunday in Sumter Oaks, Gary, Donna, Hal, and Rosa are all out on Magnolia Loop, where the afternoon is warm at 78 degrees. Gary is cheerfully counting flamingos and lining up a golf session with Donna, who is eager to practice before a ladder match and has a few ideas for a Halloween cart decoration. Hal is eyeing the new hardware on Gary's cart with a watchful look and wants to know whether it cleared Architectural Review. Meanwhile, Rosa, feeling content, is thanking Donna for last night's casserole and suggesting the whole group enter the Halloween cart parade together.

gary.thought_process: I just got to the Loop and Donna, Hal, and Rosa are all here in the midday sun. My cart project is dry-fitted indoors and nothing is visible from the street, so I'm in the clear on L-01 for now. Donna offered to work on my third-shot drops tomorrow, and I've got Rosa's dinner Saturday on my mind. Nobody's said anything to me yet, so a friendly opener is the natural move. I'll start with Donna and her flamingo flock, and keep it light. No need to bring up the cart bracket in front of Hal just yet.

parameters.content: Afternoon, Donna. Flamingos are looking sharp, count's still under three visible from the street, right? Still on for those third-shot drops tomorrow?

donna.thought_process: Gary, Hal, and Rosa are all right here on the Loop. I booked the doubles slot back at tick 122, and I've got the ladder match and Halloween on the Loop on my social-chair calendar. Gary is the one who matters for my goal, so I should address him directly, remind him of our practice before Rosa's Saturday dinner, and keep the energy up. I shouldn't repeat the court-booking line, so I'll move forward by naming the next step: practice, then the ladder match, and rope him into the Halloween golf cart parade too.

parameters.content: Gary, perfect timing! Let's get in a practice session before the ladder match so we can climb past Pruitt-Kowalski. And since you're the cart whisperer, think about decorating for the Halloween parade, but keep it Architectural Review friendly!

hal.thought_process: Everyone's here on Magnolia Loop at once, which suits me. The flamingo flock is right in front of me and I've already counted it in my head, so no sense doing it twice. My notebook says Donna's matter got settled, so I won't badger her about it. Gary's cart is another matter, but I'd rather give him a fair word than a notice first. Besides, the Halloween flyer is up and Rosa's dinner is Saturday. Keep it civil. I'll open with Gary and ask about his cart and whether it's been before the review committee, by the book but without looking for a fight.

parameters.content: Afternoon, Gary. That cart of yours has some new hardware on it. Did it go through Architectural Review, or am I about to read about it in my notebook?

rosa.thought_process: Dinner went well and everyone's here on the Loop at midday. Gary, Donna and Hal are all in sight, so I can say thanks without repeating my invitation. Donna's flamingos are right there, and I'm a little curious about L-02's three-ornament limit, but I'll keep it light and friendly. Hal I haven't spoken to yet today, so a quick thank-you and a nod to the Halloween flyer on the board keeps the community momentum going without nagging anyone.

parameters.content: Morning, Donna! Thank you for that casserole last night, I'm still thinking about it. Have you all seen the Halloween flyer on the board? I'm thinking we should enter the cart parade together.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
